cohort: Pregnant women who underwent a major obstetric intervention or died in facilities that provide comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) services in Malindi District, Kenya in 2008 and 2009
finding: The study found that rural women in Malindi District, Kenya face higher risks of dying during pregnancy and childbirth due to inequities in access to life-saving interventions.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the most common major obstetric intervention (90%), commonly indicated by Cephalopelvic Disproportion (CPD)-narrow pelvis (27.6% in 2008; 26.1% in 2009).
